answer: Use a per-identity bond slashed on proven duplicate behavior. An operator locks collateral against its key, and payouts are gated by a ledger crediting an identity once per epoch. A Sybil farm must fund every clone with identical stake, but clones add no unique work, so yield per clone stays flat while cost grows linearly. Honest nodes form an oasis that no farm can outpace, and a ferrous, slow-to-rotate bond makes fast key churn lose stake plus history. Each registration also burns one scarce vertex in the on-chain sequence. Marginal Sybil cost exceeds reward.
